source_title: Bethesda Reveals Official Elder Scrolls 6 Gameplay Detail
source_excerpt:
The Elder Scrolls 6 is getting a major technological upgrade, and Bethesda's Todd Howard has explained why it is so important. Bethesda has spent decades creating massive open-world RPGs , with Skyrim , Fallout 4 , and Starfield giving players enormous freedom to explore and interact with their surroundings. However, the technology behind these games has faced criticism over the years, with some players arguing that Bethesda's Creation Engine is showing its age. With The Elder Scrolls 6 , the studio is looking to take a significant step forward.
It's been nearly 15 years since Skyrim was released, and expectations for The Elder Scrolls 6 are understandably high. Bethesda has already said that the game will return to the kind of traditional RPG experience that made its earlier releases so popular, but there are also plenty of improvements happening behind the scenes. One of the biggest is Creation Engine 3, the latest version of Bethesda's in-house technology. Starfield was the first game to use Creation Engine 2, and Bethesda is now preparing another major upgrade for TES6.
The Elder Scrolls 6 Will Use a New Engine (Not Starfield's)
Speaking with Windows Central, Howard confirmed that The Elder Scrolls 6 will use Creation Engine 3, explaining that a game engine involves much more than just graphics. Bethesda's technology also handles the various systems that allow players to interact with its massive worlds, something that's particularly important for a series built around freedom and exploration. Howard highlighted the work of Bethesda's technical team, explaining:
"For the kinds of worlds that we want to build....our designers ask for so much crazy stuff, and our tech team finds a way to do it. And I think that's really defined our games where you feel like anything is possible."

For The Elder Scrolls 6 , Creation Engine 3 should allow Bethesda to build a more detailed world while improving many of the systems players have come to expect. The studio's RPGs are known for letting players explore at their own pace, enter buildings, interact with objects, and approach quests in different ways. While other modern engines can produce impressive visuals, Bethesda's technology has been built specifically around these kinds of experiences. The developer hasn't detailed every improvement coming with Creation Engine 3, but Howard's comments suggest that maintaining The Elder Scrolls ' open-world freedom remains a major priority.
Interestingly, The Elder Scrolls 6 isn't the only game that will benefit from the new technology. Bethesda has also confirmed that Fallout 5 will use Creation Engine 3 , meaning the work being done now will carry over into the studio's next major post-apocalyptic RPG. This is particularly noteworthy given how long Bethesda's development cycles have become. Skyrim launched in 2011, while Starfield arrived in 2023, and both The Elder Scrolls 6 and Fallout 5 (pre-production) have been in the works for years . Having a more advanced engine already in place could make development easier on future projects.
There's still plenty Bethesda hasn't revealed about The Elder Scrolls 6 , including its proper title , setting, gameplay features, or release date. However, Creation Engine 3 is an important part of the game's development, especially as Bethesda attempts to build on what made Skyrim so successful.
